title: Meta Is Cutting 8,000 Jobs Tomorrow. For Thousands of Indian Engineers on H-1B Visas, the Clock Just Started.
excerpt: The largest tech layoff of 2026 begins May 20. Inside the restructuring that will reshape Silicon Valley's biggest Indian workforce — and what it means for the visa holders who built the company.
body:
When the notifications begin rolling out at 4 AM local time on Wednesday, May 20, roughly 8,000 Meta employees worldwide will discover they no longer have jobs. An internal memo from Meta's Chief People Officer Janelle Gale, reviewed by Reuters, confirms what has been the worst-kept secret in Silicon Valley for weeks: the company is cutting 10 percent of its global workforce in its single largest round of layoffs since the brutal retrenchment of 2022-23.

But the numbers only tell part of the story. For the thousands of Indian-origin engineers who form the backbone of Meta's technical workforce — many of them on H-1B visas — May 20 is not just a bad day at the office. It is the start of a 60-day countdown that could upend their lives in America.

## The Restructuring Behind the Numbers

Meta's layoffs are not a cost-cutting panic. They are the operational expression of a strategic bet that Mark Zuckerberg has been telegraphing for over a year: the company's future runs on artificial intelligence, and the humans who built the old Meta are not necessarily the ones who will build the new one.

According to the memo, approximately 7,000 employees — nearly as many as are being let go — will be reassigned into newly created AI-focused units. The company is flattening its management layers, replacing traditional hierarchies with what Gale described as "smaller teams of pods/cohorts that can move faster and with more ownership." Managerial roles are being eliminated. The memo explicitly states that additional deep cuts are expected later in 2026.

The restructuring follows Meta's announcement of up to $135 billion in AI infrastructure spending for the year — a figure that dwarfs the payroll savings from the layoffs. Zuckerberg's vision of embedding AI agents across every Meta product, from Instagram recommendations to WhatsApp business tools, requires a fundamentally different workforce. The company wants AI-native engineers, not the mobile and web developers who powered the social media era.

## The H-1B Equation

This is where the story hits the Indian diaspora hardest. Indians consistently account for over 70 percent of H-1B visa approvals in the United States. Meta, along with Google, Amazon, and Microsoft, has been one of the top H-1B sponsors in Silicon Valley. When a company of this size cuts 10 percent of its workforce, the statistical reality is that a disproportionate number of affected workers will be Indian nationals on employer-sponsored visas.

For H-1B holders, losing a job triggers a 60-day grace period to find new sponsoring employment — a window that has become increasingly difficult to navigate in a market where every major tech company is simultaneously cutting headcount and freezing non-AI hiring. Over 81,200 tech jobs have been eliminated in 2026 alone, according to tracking data from Layoffs.fyi. Microsoft has offered voluntary buyouts. Snap cut 16 percent of its workforce. The lifeboat is crowded.

The alternative — returning to India — is not necessarily a consolation. While India's tech sector is growing, compensation at Indian companies rarely matches Silicon Valley rates. For engineers who have spent years building equity, buying homes, and enrolling children in American schools, a forced return represents a fundamental disruption to life plans that were supposed to be permanent.

## Inside Meta's AI Pivot

The internal tension at Meta runs deeper than layoffs. Over 1,000 employees recently signed a petition protesting a new AI-powered mouse-tracking software that Meta deployed internally. The tool, which monitors cursor movements and application usage, is reportedly being used to train AI models that replicate human-computer interaction patterns. Employees described it as invasive; Meta framed it as an AI development tool.

Meta CTO Andrew Bosworth followed up the layoff announcement with what staff described as an ultimatum: underperformance is "not an option" in the restructured company. The message was clear — those who survive the cuts face higher expectations, tighter teams, and a corporate culture that has shifted from the "move fast and break things" ethos to something more closely resembling a wartime footing.

## What This Means for Indian Tech

The Meta layoffs are a signal, not an anomaly. Across Silicon Valley, the AI transition is reshaping who gets hired, who gets retained, and who gets shown the door. Indian engineering talent built the infrastructure of the social media age. Whether that same talent pool adapts quickly enough to dominate the AI age is an open question — one that 8,000 people will begin confronting tomorrow morning.

For NRI families watching from India, the myth of the permanent American tech career is cracking. The question is no longer whether your son or daughter will get a job at Meta or Google. It is whether that job will still exist in two years.
